question: A shopkeeper bought an article for ₹520. At what price (in ₹) should he sell the article to make 20% profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Value of 20% in fraction = 1/5

If Cost Price is 5 parts, Profit is 1 part, so Selling Price = 6 parts.

Given 5 parts = ₹520 ⇒ 1 part = 520 ÷ 5 = ₹104

Selling Price (6 parts) = 6 × 104 = 624

**∴ The correct answer is ₹624.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = ₹520

Profit Percentage = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × [(100 + Profit%) ÷ 100]

 
 CP = ₹520 (100%)
 
 
 + 20% Profit

 SP = 120% = ₹624

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 520 × [(100 + 20) ÷ 100]

⇒ SP = 520 × (120 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP = 520 × 1.2

⇒ SP = 624

**∴ The correct answer is ₹624.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Formula

If an article is sold at a loss, the Selling Price (SP) is calculated as: SP = CP × [(100 − Loss%) ÷ 100].

Profit/Loss Base Rule

Profit and Loss percentages are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated otherwise.

Marked Price & Discount

When a discount is offered on the Marked Price (MP), the Selling Price (SP) becomes: SP = MP × [(100 − Discount%) ÷ 100].
